notes:
Context: Mid-market product org building an AI-first in-app assistant (support + knowledge base + light code assist). Currently on another LLM API provider (OpenAI) and investigating migration to Redwood for cost predictability and on-prem-ish network options. Team cares about prompt parity and avoiding regressions when switching providers. They want first to validate Hosted API parity, then migrate to Dedicated for predictable throughput and VPC isolation.

Key asks / constraints:
- Latency targets: p50 ~120-200ms for short chat turns (max 300ms p95).
- Throughput: steady 20-40 requests/s during business hours, burst to 150 req/s for ticket triage jobs.
- Cost sensitivity: moderate-high — looking to reduce per-token costs and get predictable monthly billing.
- Model preferences: open-model family preferences; need compatibility with current prompt templates and function-calling.
- Security: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS integration, and US data residency for PII traces.

Recent summary of evaluation activities:
- POC path: Hosted POC -> verify prompt parity/regressions -> Dedicated sizing & pricing -> prod migration (compat adapter if needed).
- Early Hosted POC shows good latency and ~8-12% token cost reduction with Redwood batching and prefix cache on our replay set.
- Found output differences on 4 of 120 canonical prompts (style/hallucination shifts); team flagged these as regressions for user-visible templates.
- Compatibility: they currently use an SDK wrapper around OpenAI that relies on response shape and function-calling behavior; asked for Redwood compatibility layer or migration guide.

Quotes from calls:
- "If we can't hit prompt parity within the Hosted POC, we can't move forward — too many downstream templates tied to tone and entity extraction." — Head of Product (E. Moreno).
- "Cost predictability + VPC is the main push from infra/security." — VP Eng (S. Alvarez).

POC artifacts & tech notes:
- Seed prompt corpus (internal): drive:/deals/archipelago/poc-plan.md (sample prompts + expected outputs).
- Regression triage spreadsheet: drive:/deals/archipelago/poc-regressions.csv (team maintains diffs and acceptance status).
- Requested SDK compatibility checklist from Redwood: awaiting response.

Risks / blockers (short):
- Prompt parity regressions need engineering time to triage; some require prompt engineering, others suggest model-behavior differences.
- Compatibility layer work (to match OpenAI SDK expectations) not fully scoped; devs price ~2-3 sprints if built in-house.
- Security Q still open — InfoSec needs clarifications on audit log retention and KMS key rotation policies.

Commercial notes:
- Initial interest in a Dedicated commit after 3-month Hosted POC if parity and SLAs acceptable.
- Price sensitivity around cost per token; interested in a blended committed rate for Dedicated.

Action items for Redwood reps:
- Submit SDK compatibility doc and example wrapper for OpenAI -> Redwood translation (include function-calling examples).
- Provide prompt parity report after next POC run with diffs for 120 canonical prompts.
- Set up Dedicated sizing session with infra (Ravi + Archipelago infra) to map RB metrics to GPU pools.
- Deliver answers to security questionnaire (drive:/security/archipelago/sec-answers.pdf) by 2026-03-17.
